problem: The plot contradicts the chapter's own definition of the design point. The text says the hill's peak is the design point, so each curve should be highest at Q/Q design = 1.0. Instead the Pelton series peaks at 0.7 (0.88) and drops to 0.82 at 1.0, and the caption/aria calls this 'peaks sharply near design flow'. A student would read the Pelton design flow as 0.7 Q design, and that Pelton is worse than Francis and Kaplan at full design flow.
fix: Move each series so its maximum falls at Q/Q design = 1.0, e.g. Pelton points [[0.2,0.42],[0.5,0.70],[0.7,0.82],[0.85,0.87],[1.0,0.89]], keep Francis peak near 0.9–1.0 and Kaplan flat across 0.6–1.2, and keep the caption 'the peak of each curve is the design point'.

problem: 'Muschel curves and the iso-efficiency hill collect many such tests' introduces a named curve without saying what it plots, so the reader cannot tell it apart from a main curve or an operating curve.
fix: Define it: 'A Muschel curve plots efficiency against speed ratio (or unit speed) for one fixed guide-vane opening at constant head, so a family of them shows how the best operating point shifts as the opening changes.'

problem: 'keeps the speed ratio near its best value' is the wrong variable for a Kaplan. A grid-connected Kaplan runs at fixed N and (for a given site) fixed H, so u and the speed ratio u/V are fixed; what the double adjustment preserves is the flow angle into the runner (the velocity triangles).
fix: Write: 'A Kaplan turbine has movable runner blades and guide vanes, so it re-angles the flow into the runner as Q falls and keeps the velocity triangles close to their best shape.'
